newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian refineries schedule maintenance from July.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian refineries schedule maintenance from July.

text.p: Nigerian oil refineries will undergo their overdue turnaround maintenance in the second half of the year, according to a senior oil refinery executive.

"The approved schedule now is to have Kaduna refinery go on maintenance in July, Port Harcourt in the last quarter of the year and Warri refinery in the first quarter of 1998," managing director of the Warri Refining and Petrochemical Company, Ezenwa Dennar, told reporters in Warri in the midwest at the weekend.
Dennar said the maintenance had earlier been scheduled to commence in the first quarter of this year but that this did not receive government approval.

Nigeria is currently suffering from an acute shortage of petrol even though state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation insists that the cause is not from the refineries which they say are pumping normally.
Dennar said the 125,000 barrels per day (bpd) Warri refinery was producing at 90,000 bpd or 72 percent of its capacity.
He blamed the shortfall on a reduced allocation of crude oil to the facility.
"The volume of crude oil made available to the plant is 90,000 bpd," he said, adding, "The Warri plant needs 100,000 bpd to operate at optimum level."

The government last year slashed to 250,000 bpd from 300,000 bpd the crude oil allocated to the four refineries, which have a combined output capacity of 445,000 bpd but usually operate well below that because of poor management.
